summary: Among the specialists, the only 2026 capital move aimed squarely at the public-builder lot-option business is Hearthstone: FivePoint (75% owner since mid-2025) and Blue Owl announced a programme to buy up to $1.7 billion of residential land through it, yet Hearthstone's reported AUM has sat at about $3.4 billion through FivePoint's Q3 2026 release. Forestar remains a captive of D.R. Horton rather than a competitor for third-party builders: 86% of fiscal 2026 lots went to Horton, sales to others fell to 1,916 lots, and it guides flat-to-down for fiscal 2027 with $1.3 billion of liquidity and almost no net debt. Walton Global is the most visible retail-funded entrant, buying roughly 2,100 finished or near-finished lots in H1 2026 through its Finished Lot Program and raising up to $500 million plus a $250 million credit fund, but it names no builders and its deals are small (24 to 640 lots). New and adjacent capital is arriving from builder-backed private credit (Avila Real Estate Capital's $1 billion Fund Two with D.R. Horton, Toll and Century as investors) and a Wafra/Hunt-backed start-up (Strata Land Partners, November 2026), both pitched at private builders. GTIS (renamed Brightshore Capital in September 2026) and IHP are equity JV investors, not option land bankers; Kiavi was bought by Figure for $717 million and Builders Capital is a construction lender, so neither competes for land-bank deals. Trade press in November 2026 expects option-fee and takedown re-trades in 2027, with builders resisting a 10% land-bank carry.

facts.fact: Forestar Group: at 2026-09-30 it owned about 58,200 lots and controlled about 26,200 more through purchase contracts (84,400 total). About 21,500 owned lots (37%) were under contract to sell, worth about $2.2 billion of future revenue; 19,800 of those were under contract to D.R. Horton and a further 18,600 owned lots (32%) were subject to D.R. Horton's right of first offer.
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-09-30) revenue was $1,635.1 million on 13,545 lots sold (5,004 lots and $580.8 million in Q4); pre-tax income $192.1 million, net income $142.6 million ($2.78 per diluted share). Lots sold to customers other than D.R. Horton were 1,916 in the year (822 in Q4), i.e. about 14% of lots sold (calculated: 1,916 / 13,545).
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: at 2026-09-30 liquidity was about $1.3 billion ($657.0 million unrestricted cash plus $657.8 million available on its senior unsecured revolver); debt was $794.2 million with no senior note maturity until fiscal 2028; net debt to total capital 6.7%; stockholders' equity $1,916.2 million (book value $37.56 per share, up 8% year on year).
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: fiscal 2027 guidance is 12,000 to 13,000 lots delivered and $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion of revenue, i.e. flat to down against fiscal 2026's 13,545 lots and $1.64 billion.
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: D.R. Horton owned about 62% of Forestar at 2026-09-30. Under the Master Supply Agreement Horton has a right of first offer on up to 100% of lots in Horton-sourced projects and up to 50% of lots in the first phase of Forestar-sourced projects (and 50% of later phases if it bought at least 25% of the prior phase); no right on third-party-sourced deals. The agreement runs to the earlier of Horton holding under 15% of the vote or 2037-06-29. Forestar operated in 65 markets in 24 states with 408 employees and sold fiscal 2026 lots at an average price of $111,200.
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, Item 1

facts.fact: Walton Global: on 2026-02-12 it launched The American Builder Growth and Income Fund, seeking up to $500 million through independent broker-dealers, family offices and RIAs. The fund mixes secured land loans to homebuilders (made through Walton's Builder Land Financing platform) with land acquisition for appreciation.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: launches The American Builder Growth and Income Fund

facts.fact: Walton Global: in February and March 2026 its Builder Land Finance platform closed eight properties totalling about 1,392 lots in Texas, Florida, Georgia and Arizona, seven of them through its Finished Lot Program. The six communities listed are Cascada in the Tucson area (638 lots, 105 acres), three Dallas-Fort Worth properties (366 lots combined) Bridle Creek in Jacksonville (230 lots), Indian Springs in Houston (80), South Wind in Atlanta (54) and Oakfield Trails in western Florida (24). No builder was named.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: acquires eight properties in key Sunbelt markets

facts.fact: Walton Global: AltsWire (2026-06-11) puts Walton at $4.54 billion of total assets and more than 85,000 acres under ownership, management and administration in the US and Canada, and says its Builder Land Finance Fund III (launched July 2025) is a private credit offering targeting $250 million with projected returns of 9% to 11.5%; a Shariah-compliant U.S. Land Income & Growth Fund for offshore investors followed in March 2026. Walton funds its builder programme from retail / private-wealth channels rather than institutional mandates.
facts.source_title: AltsWire: Walton Global adds 525 builder-direct lots in three states

facts.fact: Hearthstone: FivePoint Holdings bought 75% of Hearthstone Residential Holdings in mid-2025 (founder Mark Porath kept 25%); at that point Hearthstone managed over $2.6 billion and had funded more than 173,000 homes and lots. On 2026-03-02 the Orange County Business Journal reported that FivePoint and Blue Owl Capital plan to buy up to $1.7 billion of US residential land through Hearthstone: Blue Owl funds provide the capital and earn warrants on FivePoint shares at $7, vesting as contribution milestones from $500 million up to $1.7 billion are met. Hearthstone's AUM was then about $3.4 billion.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: FivePoint and Blue Owl Launch $1.7B Deal

facts.fact: Strata Land Partners: a new land-finance platform launched 2026-11-02, backed by Wafra (about $30 billion AUM) and Hunt Companies and led by Michael Forsum, former president and COO of Landsea Homes. It offers land financing and lot-development capital to public and private builders, with a stated tilt to private builders; its first projects total about 1,300 single-family lots. Committed capital was not disclosed.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Strata Land Partners launch

facts.fact: Avila Real Estate Capital (AREC): held a $100 million first close on its second builder debt fund in November 2025, anchored by Hillwood Communities, with a $1 billion target by mid-2026. It makes first-lien land development loans and homebuilder revolvers for for-sale housing only. Its first debt fund closed July 2025 with over $700 million of commitments and co-investments.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Hillwood backs new homebuilding fund as AD&C credit tightens

facts.fact: IHP Capital Partners: agreed to acquire 1,458 acres in Brazoria County, Texas (south Houston) for the Peachtree master plan, closing in phases; the first phase closed with 206 acres and 535 finished single-family lots. IHP posted the acquisition on its news page on 2026-09-30; reported by IREI on 2026-11-03 in an interview with co-president Richard Whiteley, who said the firm uses uncertain periods to secure land in high-growth markets. (Only the article's free opening was readable.)
facts.source_title: IREI: IHP Capital Partners sees long-term housing opportunities amid near-term market uncertainty

facts.fact: Forestar Group: of 13,545 lots sold in fiscal 2026 (down 5% from 14,240), 1,916 went to customers other than D.R. Horton (2,489 in fiscal 2025); that 1,916 includes 146 lots sold for $33.4 million to a lot banker that expects to resell them to Horton (927 such lots in fiscal 2025). Horton therefore took about 11,629 lots directly, 86% (calculated: 13,545 less 1,916). Only 116 lots came from Forestar's own short-term 'lot banking projects' (348 in fiscal 2025).
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, MD&A

facts.fact: Forestar Group: capital structure at 2026-09-30 was a $715 million senior unsecured revolver (undrawn; $57.2 million of letters of credit; uncommitted accordion to $1 billion; $650 million matures 2029-12-18, $65 million matured 2026-10-28; commitments raised $25 million in October 2025 and $50 million in March 2026), $300 million of 5.0% senior notes due 2028-03-01 and $500 million of 6.5% senior notes due 2033-03-15. A $750 million equity shelf (including a $300 million at-the-market program) was untouched in fiscal 2026.
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, debt and equity notes

facts.fact: Forestar Group: fiscal 2026 investment was $270.1 million to acquire residential land and about $1.0 billion to develop it. Only about 8,100 of its 58,200 owned lots were fully developed at 2026-09-30 (8,900 a year earlier).
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, MD&A

facts.fact: Forestar Group: Executive Chairman Donald J. Tomnitz retired effective 2026-10-31 (staying as a paid strategic adviser to 2028-09-30). President and CEO Anthony W. Oxley became Executive Chairman as well on 2026-11-01, as D.R. Horton's designee. Stacey H. Dwyer, a former D.R. Horton EVP and Treasurer (1991-2014), joined the board on 2026-11-01 as a Horton designee.
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Item 5.02 dated 2026-10-28

facts.fact: Hearthstone: FivePoint's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-22) still shows about $3.4 billion of Hearthstone assets under management. Hearthstone segment management-fee revenue was $6.5 million in Q3 2026 and $18.2 million for the nine months; segment pre-tax profit was $3.0 million and $7.8 million. The release gives no figure for capital funded under the Blue Owl programme.
facts.source_title: Five Point Holdings 8-K Ex. 99.1, Q3 2026 results (2026-10-22)

facts.fact: Hearthstone: Orange County Business Journal (2026-03-02) reported that in the first five months under FivePoint, Hearthstone earned $11.8 million of management fees and contributed $3.5 million of net income, and that FivePoint expected $300 million to $500 million of new capital commitments in Q1 2026.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: FivePoint and Blue Owl Launch $1.7B Deal

facts.fact: GTIS Partners: on 2026-04-08 GTIS and Hovnanian Enterprises announced a $200 million homebuilding joint venture: GTIS vehicles put in $150 million and Hovnanian $50 million (25%). It covers seven for-sale communities in five states with about 907 homes left to deliver, about $545 million of projected build-out cost and about $617 million of home value; 125 homes (about $82 million) were sold but not closed at closing. This is an equity JV on communities already under construction, not a lot-option land bank. The announcement says it takes the GTIS-Hovnanian portfolio to $1.5 billion and the JV platform to about $8 billion of total home value.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: GTIS-Hovnanian JV announcement

facts.fact: Avila Real Estate Capital (AREC): by 2026-09-01 it had provided a $305 million facility to an unnamed California master-plan developer (more than 3,000 lots; horizontal and vertical funding; about $700 million across two AREC financings to that borrower), syndicated to banks and family offices in Israel, Brazil, Kuwait and Japan. Tony Avila said Fund Two had reached its $1 billion target; named investors in it include D.R. Horton, Toll Brothers, Century Communities, LGI Homes, Dream Finders Homes and DRB Group. AREC says it has financed more than 18,000 lots against a goal of 100,000 in five years.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: AREC $305M California land facility

facts.fact: Builder lending market: NAHB survey averages for Q2 2026, as cited by The Builder's Daily on 2026-09-01, were about 10.43% for land acquisition loans, 12.59% for land development loans and 11.82% for speculative single-family construction loans (effective rates). Useful as the bank / private-credit alternative a builder compares a land-bank option fee against.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: AREC $305M California land facility

facts.fact: Walton Global: sold 35 acres (198 lots) in Phase 2 of its Lake Ridge Parkway master plan in Ellis County, Texas (Dallas-Fort Worth) to Meritage Homes; price not disclosed. Reported 2026-07-16.
facts.source_title: AltsWire: Walton Global sells 35 acres to Meritage Homes at Lake Ridge Parkway

facts.fact: Kiavi: closed a $350 million rated securitization of residential transition loans on 2026-02-19 (its sixth rated deal and 24th on the LHOME shelf; two-year revolving period; rated by Morningstar DBRS; more than 5x oversubscribed), projected to add about $1.2 billion of funding capacity. Kiavi reports record 2025 originations of $7.8 billion (up 20%) and more than $30 billion funded to date. Its business is fix-and-flip / bridge loans to investors plus a ground-up construction product; nothing found on land banking or lot financing for homebuilders.
facts.source_title: Kiavi press release: closes $350M rated RTL securitization

facts.fact: Walton Global: its own release (2026-06-12) confirms eight Finished Lot Program closings in April and May 2026 totalling 525 lots: Houston 247 lots (Baron Village 183, Magnolia Meadows at Holly Ridge 40, Williams Reserve East 24), Dallas-Fort Worth 103 (Wildcat Ranch 50, Bluestem 53), Wellen Park, Florida 123 (Palmera 47, Edgewater 76) and Riverlake in the Wilmington, NC area 52. Deal sizes are 24 to 183 lots; no builder is named.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: strengthens land portfolio with acquisitions across key southern growth regions

facts.fact: Walton Global: the 64-lot Sarasota purchase (expanding Oakfield Lakes, Finished Lot Program, release dated 2026-02-23) is one of four 2026 lot announcements. Calculated from Walton's own releases: 130 (Gemini, January) + 64 (Sarasota, February) + about 1,392 (February-March batch) + 525 (April-May batch) = about 2,111 lots acquired January to May 2026. The Sarasota lots may overlap with the February-March batch, so treat about 2,100 as an upper estimate.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: acquisition of 64 residential lots in Sarasota

facts.fact: Walton Global: 130 residential lots acquired at the Gemini community in Splendora, Texas through the Finished Lot Program, announced 2026-01-27; no builder, price or takedown schedule disclosed.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: expands Texas presence with newest acquisition near Houston

facts.fact: Walton Global: its Builder Land Financing page describes the structure only in outline: Walton buys land identified by a homebuilder client, charges the builder a premium, pays investors current interest semi-annually or quarterly and returns principal pro rata as homes are built and sold ('just-in-time' inventory). No fee rate, deposit or takedown terms are published.
facts.source_title: Walton Global: Builder Land Financing page

facts.fact: Walton Global: sold about 245 acres of its Lee Farm (Pinecrest) master plan in Loveland, Colorado to Forestar Group (release dated 2025-08-07); the plan is about 1,016 homes at build-out and Forestar is to deliver finished lots to D.R. Horton. Price not disclosed. Shows Walton acting as land seller to Horton's lot developer as well as financier.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: sells 245 acres to Forestar in Loveland, Colorado

facts.fact: GTIS Partners: renamed itself Brightshore Capital (reported 2026-09-15) after buying out minority partner GoldenTree Asset Management in 2025; about $5.6 billion of assets. It launched its first dedicated debt vehicle with an initial $250 million, aimed at multifamily / rental residential credit (preferred equity, mezzanine, stretch senior, B-notes). The article does not mention for-sale homebuilding or land.
facts.source_title: Bisnow: GTIS Partners rebrands as Brightshore Capital, launches $250M debt platform

facts.fact: IHP Capital Partners: its 2025-2026 news flow is equity joint ventures with private builders and master-plan development, not lot-option land banking. Items on its news page: townhome JVs with The Grupe Company (San Ramon, 2.5 acres, posted 2025-09-18; Pleasanton, 2.6 acres, posted 2026-11-04) and Intracorp Homes (Alhambra, 2 acres, 2025-04-28); a first for-sale community with Onyx+East in Westfield, Indiana (2026-05-15); and the 1,458-acre Peachtree acquisition in Brazoria County, Texas (posted 2026-09-30).
facts.source_title: IHP Capital Partners: news page

facts.fact: IHP Capital Partners: joint venture with Indianapolis builder Onyx+East for Trillium, an $80 million, 119-home community on 44 acres in Westfield, Indiana (base prices about $630,000 to $856,000; land about $116,000 to $120,000 per acre ready to build). Site closing and JV were announced May 2026. The article says IHP has completed 44 housing projects in Orange County and has also invested in Indianapolis, Cincinnati and Columbus.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: IHP Expands Beyond Orange County with $80M Indiana Project

facts.fact: Hearthstone: its website still describes three lines: land banking and model sale-leaseback for public builders, joint-venture financing for private builders (up to 97% of the capital) and advisory; it claims over $18.0 billion committed to for-sale homebuilding across more than 700 communities. The site's newest news item is from 2024 and it does not mention FivePoint or Blue Owl, so it is stale against the 2025-2026 filings.
facts.source_title: Hearthstone website home page

facts.fact: Builders Capital: describes itself as a residential construction lender (tradename of Construction Loan Services II, LLC, part of the Builders Capital Exchange / BCX network; Puyallup, Washington). Products are an all-in-one acquisition, development and construction facility, new-construction lines, build-to-rent and bridge loans; it claims $17 billion+ of projects financed, 500+ builders, 18,000+ homes, 15,000+ lots developed and exposure of up to $350 million per builder. It does not offer lot-option land banking.
facts.source_title: Builders Capital website home page

facts.fact: Kiavi: Figure Technology Solutions agreed on 2026-06-10 to buy Kiavi's technology and operating platform in a $717 million transaction ($538 million from Figure, funded by a $600 million senior unsecured notes issue; $179 million from Sixth Street, whose joint venture with Figure buys Kiavi's balance-sheet loans). Kiavi had more than $250 million of revenue and more than $100 million of EBITDA in the prior year and has funded more than $30 billion of loans. Its products are investor fix-and-flip (RTL) and DSCR rental loans, so it is not a competitor for builder land.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Figure bolsters first-lien strategy with $717M deal for Kiavi

facts.fact: Kiavi: HousingWire reported on 2026-09-01 that Figure had completed the $717 million Kiavi acquisition; Kiavi continues as a Figure subsidiary and CEO Arvind Mohan joined Figure as chief business officer.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Figure completes Kiavi deal, adds investor loans to blockchain platform

facts.fact: Builder lending market: NAHB's Q3 2026 AD&C survey, as reported 2026-11-13, put effective borrowing costs (contract rate plus points, annualised) at 10.55% for land acquisition, 11.69% for land development, 11.83% for speculative single-family construction and 11.47% for pre-sold construction; contract rates were 8.08%, 7.83%, 7.72% and 7.27%. Credit tightened for a 19th straight quarter (NAHB net easing index -15.3; Fed -15.5).
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Builder credit conditions tighten for 19th straight quarter

facts.fact: Land banking market: consultant Scott Cox (SLC Advisors) wrote on 2026-11-18 that 2027 will be a land negotiation year: builders may refuse to pay a land banker a 10% carry and may instead offer sellers rolling takedowns with a 3% annual escalator; he expects 'meaningful re-trades, not just extensions', especially for newer land bankers, and expects land prices (not only terms) to correct. Opinion piece, not disclosed deal terms.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Why 2027 may turn into a land negotiation year for homebuilders

facts.fact: Land banking market: Launch DFA's sponsored article of 2026-05-20 cites roughly 12% as the industry cost of funding through private land-bank funds, contrasted with Millrose's lower cost of capital.
facts.source_title: HousingWire sponsored content (Launch DFA): infrastructure finance and land banking

facts.fact: Century Communities bought Texas builder HistoryMaker Homes (reported 2026-10-13) while the selling Mitchell family kept its land developer, Jabez Development, which will keep developing selected communities for Century; no economics disclosed. A seller-retained developer acting as lot supplier is an alternative to third-party land banking.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Why the Mitchells sold the builder but kept the land platform

facts.fact: Hearthstone: reported assets under management were about $3.4 billion in March 2026 (OCBJ) and still about $3.4 billion in FivePoint's Q3 2026 release of 2026-10-22, up from over $2.6 billion at the mid-2025 acquisition. Inference from those two sources: AUM grew about 30% in the first months under FivePoint and has been flat through the first nine months of 2026 despite the $1.7 billion Blue Owl programme.
facts.source_title: Five Point Holdings 8-K Ex. 99.1, Q3 2026 results (compared with OCBJ 2026-03-02)

builder_relationships.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: GTIS-Hovnanian JV announcement

gaps: Web search budget for this run (shared across agents) was exhausted after about 15 searches, so the wider candidate list could not be checked. NOT researched at all (no finding either way): Landsea / Lot Bank-type vehicles, Raven / Rockpoint, Sumitomo Forestry / Crescent, Columnar Investments, Lotus Capital Partners, Tricon, BTI Partners, Toll Brothers' and Taylor Morrison's named land-bank partners, ResiBuilt / Pretium, Bain / Arch-type JVs, AmeriFirst, Trez Capital (trezcapital.com/news returned 404), Texas Capital / Western Alliance / Flagstar builder finance, Anchor Loans, CoreVest, Roc360, Toorak, Rialto, Emerald, JEN Partners, McCourt, Resmark, Presidio Residential Capital, Tavistock, Castle Rock, MSD / BDT, Sagebrook. These need a follow-up pass.

Walton Global: no builder is named in any 2026 Finished Lot Program / Builder Land Finance release; option premium, deposit and takedown terms are not published. The phrase 'exit-focused' was not found on the pages opened. Builder Land Finance Fund III ($250 million target, 9% to 11.5% projected return, launched July 2025) is cited only via AltsWire; the BusinessWire original (businesswire.com/news/home/20250717509861) returned 403, as did GlobeSt's piece on the $500 million fund.

Walton Global: total builder-land-finance volume to date (lots, dollars, number of builders) not publicly disclosed on its site; the $4.54 billion total assets / 85,000 acres figures come from AltsWire, not a Walton page opened in this run.

Hearthstone: capital actually funded under the Blue Owl programme, number of builders and projects, option-fee rates and named builder counterparties for 2025-2026 are not disclosed in FivePoint's Q3 2026 release or the OCBJ article. The FivePoint acquisition price is reported inconsistently ($56.25 million in a June 2025 Builder's Daily piece citing SEC filings vs $59.25 million in OCBJ, March 2026); FivePoint's 10-Q/10-K was not opened to settle it.
